jobs.occupation: Sygeplejerske til Hjemmesygeplejen i Halsnæs Kommune
jobs.description:
Får du energi af at arbejde med mennesker, der har mange komplekse sygeplejefaglige problemstillinger? 

Er du god til at holde det faglige overblik og kan du holde en god struktur i dokumentationen? Vi arbejder aktuelt på at styrke vores overblik i dokumentationen og første sygeplejefaglige vurdering. Vi har også fokus på at styrke sygeplejegruppens faglige fællesskab.

Er du god til at være faglig tovholder for borgernes forløb i et tæt tværfagligt samarbejde i faste teams? Hjemmeplejen arbejder aktuelt på samarbejdet i tværfaglige faste teams.

Er du vild med at have stor indflydelse på din vagtplan og kun et lille antal aften- eller nattevagter om måneden?
Hvis du kan se dig selv i noget af dette så læs videre

Vi er en stor gruppe dygtige og dedikerede sygeplejersker, der holder til midt i Frederiksværk i vores eget lille hus. Kom gerne forbi og mærk stemningen hos os.
Hvad kan du få hos os?

• Vi besøger borger en ad gangen og har altid blot den enkelte borger i fokus, enten i sygeplejeklinik eller i borgers hjem.
• Høj grad af selvtilrettelæggelse og indflydelse på daglige arbejdsopgaver – vi har ansvar for  egne borgere som kontaktsygeplejerske.
• En bredt sammensat kollegagruppe - både aldersmæssigt og fagligt - vi er gode til at dele viden med hinanden og bruger hinanden meget på tværs af forskelligheder.
• Løbende vidensdeling/fagligt fokus – og vi investerer i kompetenceudvikling for både den enkelte og for gruppen. ”Hos os sikrer vi en høj og vedvarende faglighed i gruppen, og der er stort fokus på tryghed i at varetage en opgave hos borger. Vi hjælper hinanden med, blandt andet, de borgere som kræver højspecialiseret behandling og pleje." 
• Nærværende og flad ledelsesstruktur hvor der ikke er langt fra idé til handling. Vi fokuserer på det der virker i praksis og har en åben dialog, så samarbejdet er bedst muligt.
• Høj trivsel hos sygeplejegruppen.
• At vi løfter i flok. ”Vi er alle tilknyttet et team af kollegaer, og man er aldrig rigtig ”alene” i den forstand, at man ALTID kan sparre med kollegaer, som har mange års erfaring inden for forskellige specialer, fx sårpleje, palliation, diabetes. 
• Personalegoder: eks. yoga/fitness for 15 kr./mdr. og adgang til booking af sommerhuse. 
• Sociale arrangementer af forskellig karakter: fx bowling, drinksaften, brætspilaften,  sommerfest, vinterbadning, fredagscafé, julefrokost etc. ”Vi vægter det sociale enten i fritiden eller i pauserne”. ”Vi har en god tone og er gode til at grine sammen”.
• Grundig introduktion med planlagt undervisning og mentorordning, der tilrettelægges ud fra dine behov.
• Mulighed for kurset ”Godt fra start i primær sektor” på Københavns Professionshøjskole i Hillerød inden for det første år, hvor du får et god viden om samarbejdspartnere når du arbejder i primær sektor.Hvad kan du byde ind med?

• En kollega, der arbejder for borgers bedste og på at få alt til at gå op i en højere enhed.
• At du er god til at arbejde struktureret og selvstændigt, og er god til at prioritere i den faglige opgavemængde.
• At du kan og vil arbejde professionelt - ud fra en fælles ramme for arbejdet og kan skabe den til tider kreative løsning for borger.
• At du evner tydelig kommunikation i øjenhøjde, både i forhold til borgere og dine kollegaer.
• At du er medspiller i mono og tværfaglige samarbejder.
• At du har lysten til at udvikle dig i fællesskab med dine kollegaer.
• At du byder ind i vores gode arbejdsmiljø og kender din egen indvirken på dette.Vi vil gerne møde dig.

Vi har meget mere at fortælle, så ring endelig og hør nærmere, eller ring og lav en aftale om at kigge forbi til kaffe og rundvisning.

Sygeplejerske/TR Cristina Arboe tlf. 2941617, sygeplejerske /AMR Zitta Sommer tlf. 29128841.

Områdeleder Cille Boysen Rønde tlf. 29625203.
Yderligere oplysninger

Timeantal: 30-37 timer om ugen eller efter aftale.

Vagterne er fortrinsvis dagvagt, med få aften- eller nattevagter om måneden. Der er også mulighed for flere nattevagter, hvis du har et ønske om det.

Ansøgningsfrist: 14.12 kl. 12.

Samtaler afholdes løbende.

Start: Efter aftale.

Løn- og ansættelsesvilkår fastsættes i henhold til gældende overenskomst. Derudover kan der aftales kvalifikations- og funktionstillæg.

Den forventede grundløn for 37 timer ligger i niveauet 32.269 - 37.657 kr. pr. måned ekskl. pension, afhængigt af erfaring og kompetencer. Hertil kommer vagttillæg.
Bliv en del af Halsnæs – et godt sted at arbejde og et godt sted at bo

Vi er en moderne og rummelig arbejdsplads med cirka 3.000 kollegaer, der hver dag gør sig umage for at levere velfærd og service af høj kvalitet. Vores værdier – redelighed, mulighed og helhed – er fundamentet for alt, vi gør. 

Hos Halsnæs Kommune arbejder vi tæt på natur, hav og fjord – og med hovedstaden inden for rækkevidde. Her får du ikke kun et spændende job, men også muligheden for at skabe et liv med ro, fællesskab og aktive oplevelser. Mange vælger at bosætte sig her for at få mere plads, nærhed til naturen og et stærkt lokalt sammenhold.

Vil du vide mere om, hvordan det er at arbejde i Halsnæs Kommune? Besøg vores hjemmeside eller vores LinkedIn-profil. 
Vil du vide mere om, hvordan det er at bo og leve i Halsnæs? Besøg Flyt til Halsnæs og se, hvad området kan tilbyde dig og din familie.

jobs.occupation: Are you at your best when others are winding down? Join NORMAL's evening team in Hedensted
jobs.description:
A busy warehouse doesn't stop when the afternoon ends and neither does the team at NORMAL's warehouse in Hedensted.

We are looking for reliable and motivated warehouse employees who want to become part of the evening shift.

This job is for you if you enjoy an active workday, like having clear goals and take pride in delivering a stable performance – shift after shift.

You will become part of a team where everyone has an important role. We depend on each other, which means reliability, responsibility and a positive attitude really matter.

What will you be doing?

Your main tasks will include:

• Picking and packing goods using a handheld scanner

• Handling and moving goods throughout the warehouse

• Operating a runner – previous experience is a strong advantage

• Maintaining an efficient and consistent work pace

• Helping your team achieve the evening's targets

The work is physical and the pace is high, so you should enjoy an active job where you are on the move.

What makes a great NORMAL warehouse employee?

It's not only about being fast.

It's about being consistent.

We are looking for colleagues who:

• Show up reliably and are ready to work

• Deliver a stable effort throughout the entire shift

• Are flexible when tasks and priorities change

• Take responsibility for their own work

• Understand and respect performance expectations

• Can receive feedback professionally and use it to improve

• Work efficiently without compromising quality

• Support their colleagues and contribute to the team

Previous warehouse experience, especially within picking and packing, is preferred. Experience operating a runner or similar warehouse equipment is a significant advantage.

You will always know what is expected

NORMAL's warehouse works with clear picking targets and performance expectations.

Productivity and work pace are followed throughout the shift. This creates transparency: you know what is expected, how you are performing and where you can improve.

For the right person, that's motivating.

We expect you to take feedback seriously, take ownership of your performance and work towards delivering consistent results.

In return, you get a workplace with clear expectations and the opportunity to show what you can do.

Your working hours – Evening Shift

Monday – Thursday: 15:00 – 23:00

Friday: 14:30 – 22:00

Your shift includes a 20-minute paid break and a 30-minute unpaid break.

What do we offer?

• DKK 173.60 per hour

• Holiday pay, pension and optional-choice account (Fritvalg)

• Employment according to applicable collective agreements

• An active job where no two shifts feel slow

• Clear goals and ongoing feedback

• Great colleagues and strong teamwork

• Experience from a large and growing company

• Possibility of long-term employment for candidates who consistently perform well

Ready to become part of the evening team?

If you're the person your colleagues can rely on – someone who shows up, stays engaged, takes responsibility and delivers a consistent effort – we want to hear from you.

Apply today and show us what you can bring to the team.

Interviews are held on an ongoing basis.

Working through JKS

As a temporary employee through JKS, you are employed under applicable collective agreements, ensuring fair working conditions and timely salary payments.

Temporary employment also gives you valuable experience and can open the door to permanent opportunities. Many companies recruit directly from their temporary workforce, making this a great opportunity to demonstrate your skills and reliability.

Normal

Om virksomheden

Hos NORMAL sælger vi helt normale varer til unormale priser. Sortimentet omfatter kendte mærkevarer inden for fx hudpleje, hårpleje, tandpleje, shampoo, makeup og rengøring. Kort sagt: Alle de ting som du ikke kan undvære i din hverdag, og som helst ikke må mangle på hylderne derhjemme. Alle varer sælges til faste, lave priser, og det betyder, at du ikke kan finde slagtilbud og prisbaskere hos os. Til gengæld kan vi love dig, at der er masser af nye og spændende varer på hylderne.

NORMAL er nemlig meget mere end faste, lave priser på kendte mærkevarer. Vores mål er, at det altid skal være en ny og unik oplevelse at besøge en af vores butikker. Også selvom det kun er en uge siden, du sidst var forbi butikken. Derfor er der i NORMAL - ud over det faste sortiment af kendte mærkevarer - hele tiden løbende udskiftning på hylder og podier, så der altid er nye varer at opdage. Vores butikslabyrint inviterer til at gå på skattejagt blandt de mange spændende varer fra kendte og ukendte brands, og det er nemt at fylde indkøbsnettet - uden at tømme bankkontoen.

Global Inventory Management Lead

Location: Høje Taastrup, Denmark

Employment type: Full time

Your impact begins here

As Global Inventory Management Lead, you will lead the inventory process within Inbound Global Supplier Operations, ensuring healthy inventory levels that support material availability, operational requirements and working capital objectives.

Working closely with planning teams, procurement, central warehouses and site teams, you will shape forecasting, material segmentation, safety stock and inventory settings. A key part of your impact will be creating an end-to-end inventory cockpit that gives stakeholders one shared view across central and site warehouses and enables coordinated decisions on replenishment, allocation and inventory balancing.

What you'll bring

You bring substantial Supply Chain and inventory management experience together with the ability to provide functional leadership across organisational boundaries. You can turn inventory insights into action, build strong relationships and create the alignment needed to move priorities forward.

• More than 8 years of Supply Chain experience, with demonstrated experience in inventory management and a proven ability to improve inventory performance.

• Demonstrated ability to provide functional leadership and deliver results through cross-functional collaboration and influence.

• Experience leading forecasting processes, material segmentation, and inventory improvement initiatives.

• Strong understanding of safety stock methodologies, replenishment planning, and inventory management across multiple warehouse locations.

• Experience developing inventory dashboards or performance cockpits and translating insights into business actions.

• Strong working knowledge of ERP or planning systems and Microsoft Excel; experience with business intelligence tools is an advantage.

• Ability to balance material availability, operational needs, and working capital objectives.

• Strong communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills.

• Ability to build solid relationships across functions, create alignment, and drive initiatives and decisions forward.

• A structured approach to problem-solving, prioritisation, and performance follow-up.

• CPIM certification preferred.

• A relevant qualification in supply chain management, logistics, business, or a related field is an advantage.

What you'll do

You will take functional leadership of inventory management within Global Supplier Operations. Your responsibilities span the full inventory process and involve close collaboration across Supply Chain:

• Lead the inventory process within Global Supplier Operations, establishing clear standards, priorities, ownership, and performance expectations.

• Lead the forecasting process in close collaboration with planning teams, incorporating material demand, business inputs, and forecast performance.

• Lead material segmentation and translate findings into differentiated inventory and replenishment strategies based on demand patterns, variability, value, and material criticality.

• Define and regularly review safety stock in close collaboration with planning teams, considering demand uncertainty, supplier performance, lead-time variability, and inventory across central and site warehouses.

• Own and continuously improve inventory settings, including reorder points, minimum and maximum stock levels, and replenishment parameters, ensuring they remain aligned with demand and operational requirements.

• Build capability through coaching, knowledge sharing, and consistent application of inventory management practices.

• Create and own an end-to-end inventory cockpit, consolidating inventory, supply and demand data across sites, while aligning stakeholders on common metrics and actions to prevent shortages and reduce slow-moving, excess and obsolete inventory.

Who you'll work with

You will work within Inbound Global Supplier Operations and collaborate closely with planning teams, procurement, central warehouses and site teams across Supply Chain.

Success in this role will depend on your ability to build trusted relationships across these functions and bring different perspectives together. Through the end-to-end inventory cockpit, you will help stakeholders work from a shared view of inventory and turn insights into coordinated decisions on replenishment, stock allocation and inventory balancing across locations.

What you can expect here

This is a functional leadership role with an opportunity to shape inventory management across Supply Chain. You will have the scope to establish consistent practices, create transparency and help teams make better, faster inventory decisions. Your work will support improved material availability, reduced excess and obsolete inventory and better working capital performance.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600 to 1,091,600 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy.

The role includes approximately 20 travel days per year.

Behind every dose of life-changing medicine is an environment that has to be exactly right. As our new HVAC Responsible, you will keep the air handling systems behind two API production facilities running reliably today, and help shape how they perform tomorrow, protecting the stable production environment that gets medicines to people living with serious chronic diseases. If you enjoy combining technical insight with stakeholder collaboration in a GMP environment, this could be your next opportunity. Apply today!

**

What you’ll do**

As HVAC Responsible, you will ensure the integrity and compliance of the HVAC systems supporting our API manufacturing facilities. You will be the point of contact for HVAC in 25K together with close colleagues, balancing the daily needs of older systems with the work of building a stronger setup for the future. Your daily tasks will be:

• Ensure daily operation of the HVAC systems that supply two production facilities in the same building, and solve problems quickly when they occur.

• Carry out routine inspection rounds and condition assessments, and upgrade ageing or faulty equipment before it affects production.

• Lead improvement projects for exchanging and maintaining the AHU systems.

• Work with UDF and LAF units, including installation support, systematic problem solving and documentation.

• Help create the future state of the HVAC systems in 25K, turning what you see on the floor into clear priorities.

You will work closely with Servicecenter Hillerød on day-to-day operations and shutdown maintenance, with Environmental Support on troubleshooting, impact assessments and knowledge sharing, and with the project team to scope and implement improvements across the facilities.

You will succeed in this role by combining your technical HVAC expertise with a pragmatic, resilient and collaborative mindset. You keep daily operations stable while moving long-term improvements forward, turn complex challenges into practical solutions, and speak up when something stalls, agreeing the next step with the people involved to keep the work moving.

What you’ll bring

We are looking for a proactive professional who knows HVAC inside out, stays calm and structured when systems need attention, and takes pride in keeping complex systems compliant and running smoothly. You also bring:

• An educational background as Maskinmester, engineer or another relevant discipline.

• Solid HVAC experience, including operating, maintaining and troubleshooting air handling units (AHU).

• Experience from the pharmaceutical industry or a similar regulated environment.

• Good collaboration, coordination and planning skills, with the ability to keep several tasks and stakeholders moving across operations, maintenance and projects.

Useful, but not essential:

• Training as Engineering Responsible (ER).

• Technical expertise in regulating pressure cascades.

• Experience with BMS and FMS.

As a person, you are robust and solution-oriented, and confident in a dynamic production environment where priorities can shift and compliance remains essential.

Who you’ll work with

You will join 25K Facility Support in API Manufacturing – a part of Global Manufacturing & Supply (GMS). In GMS we cover the full value chain from drug and device development to marketed Novo products.

25K Facility Support is a multipurpose environment that serves both existing marketed products and products on their way to market. The department supports two separate production facilities, giving you exposure to a broad range of qualification challenges and the opportunity to contribute across multiple product stages.

What you can expect hereYou will work in an international environment where your expertise is valued, and your contribution can shape decisions across areas. You will be supported to perform at your best, trusted to take ownership and empowered to drive projects forward. You will be encouraged to make your voice heard, learn from colleagues and contribute to work that helps create progress for people living with serious chronic diseases. We foster a collaborative culture where we care for one another, value initiative and support your professional growth.

What we offer

There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordinary results we produce. Being part of a global healthcare company means opportunities to learn and develop are all around us, while our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind.

As Associate Director Drug Substance Outsourcing, you will lead the team that safeguards the quality of externally manufactured drug substance for medicines in development. You will translate the department’s direction into clear priorities, strengthen your team’s capabilities, and ensure consistent, risk-based quality oversight across the portfolio. Working closely with CDMOs and CMC colleagues, you will support the timely progression of development milestones while ensuring product quality and GMP compliance for the people who may one day depend on these medicines.

What you’ll bring

You are a quality leader who takes ownership, makes decisions and inspires others to follow. You thrive in a fast-moving, complex stakeholder environment and deliver results through people. You will bring:

· A master’s degree or equivalent in pharmacy, chemistry, biotechnology, chemical engi-neering or a related discipline.

· Solid pharmaceutical QA experience and a strong understanding of GMP requirements rel-evant to drug substance manufacturing.

· Experience with outsourced manufacturing, CDMO collaboration or quality oversight of external partners.

· A track record of leading and motivating people, setting ambitious goals and building a high-performing, inclusive team culture.

· The ability to make well-founded risk-based decisions, cut through complexity and com-municate clear recommendations to technical colleagues and management.

· Strong stakeholder management skills, cross-cultural awareness and professional fluency in English.

· Comfort working with international partners and travelling when required.

Useful, but not essential:

· Experience supporting drug substance development, technology transfer or process vali-dation.

What you’ll do

· Lead a team that provides quality assurance oversight of external drug substance manu-facturing within CMC, combining decisive leadership with sound quality judgement.

· Inspire, coach and challenge the Drug Substance Outsourcing team, setting ambitious goals, balancing workload and resources.

· Drive risk-based QA oversight of external drug substance manufacturers, with clear quality responsibilities, effective governance and constant inspection readiness.

· Own quality agreements, deviations, change controls, and corrective and preventive actions within the team’s remit, ensuring timely decision-making and escalation of critical issues

· Partner with CMC colleagues and CDMOs on outsourced drug substance activities, including technology transfers and manufacturing process changes, ensuring appropriate QA involvement to support timely project execution

· Be the voice of Quality in partner governance meetings and project forums, aligning stake-holders on quality risks, priorities and actions.

· Challenge the status quo and improve team processes and ways of working, using quality performance insights to solve recurring issues.

Who you’ll work with

Drug Substance Outsourcing is part of CMC Outsourcing Quality within CMC Development Quality, in Enterprise IT & Quality. The department provides quality oversight of Novo Nordisk’s global external manufacturing partners across drug substance and clinical trial materials.

You will report to the Director of Outsourcing Quality and lead the Drug Substance Outsourcing team. Your closest partners will be colleagues across CMC Development Quality, CMC, Regulatory Affairs and other relevant functions, as well as the CDMOs you oversee globally.

Together, you will build trusted partnerships with external partners, raise quality risks early, and develop pragmatic quality approaches that support an evolving development portfolio.

What you can expect here

You will have the opportunity to shape a specialised team and make your mark on how Novo works with external drug substance manufacturers. You will be trusted to make decisions, given room to lead with ambition, and able to grow through collaboration across a global organisation with a shared focus on quality and the needs of the people we serve.

Help build the organisation that will bring new manufacturing facilities from project to operation. What you'll bring

You bring a collaborative approach to leadership and help people find clarity and make progress in a changing environment. You can translate project requirements into practical priorities, plan proactively meeting upcoming challenges and connect different teams around a shared goal.

To succeed in this role, you have:

• Experience leading and developing employees, including setting goals, providing direction and supporting individual development.

• Relevant education or practical experience within pharmaceutical production, engineering, management or a related field.

• Experience from pharmaceutical manufacturing or another regulated production environment.

• Strong communication, planning and stakeholder-management skills.

• The ability to structure priorities, maintain an overview and ensure progress in a dynamic project environment.

It would be an advantage if you also have:

• Knowledge of Good Manufacturing Practice, quality management and LEAN or cLEAN principles.

• Experience with recruitment, onboarding, training or competence development.

• Experience with operational readiness or production ramp-up.

What you'll do

• Build and lead the production team in line with project milestones and operational-readiness plans.

• Recruit, onboard, train and qualify operators and other team members according to the agreed ramp-up plan.

• Set clear priorities, roles and expectations while supporting each team member’s development, contribution and well-being.

• Ensure that the required capacity and capabilities are available for testing, qualification, validation and ramp-up activities.

• Work closely with project, production and support teams to align priorities, resources and timelines.

Who you'll work with

You will join our API IO M2 Manufacturing organisation in Kalundborg and work across both the project organisation and the future production organisation.

Your closest partners will include colleagues in Operational Readiness, Large Projects and the manufacturing leadership team. You will also collaborate with associate managers, operators and specialists within Quality, Process Support, Business Support, Training, cLEAN and Work Permit activities.

Together, you will build a strong connection between project and operations and prepare Fermentation II and Recovery III for future manufacturing. Your role will be important in creating shared priorities, clear ownership and effective collaboration throughout the transition.

What you can expect here

This role gives you the opportunity to shape a new team and influence how future manufacturing operations are established. You will work in a dynamic project environment where priorities develop as the organisation moves closer to production.

You will have the scope to make day-to-day leadership decisions, establish effective ways of working and support people in building new skills. Your contribution will have a direct impact on organisational readiness and a safe, efficient and compliant production start-up.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy.

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS) and the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy (FKF) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) seek an outstanding candidate to fill a tenure track Fellow (Assistant Professor level) position in the field of Medicinal Chemistry or a closely related discipline. The candidate is expected to start on 01.08.2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

 

We are looking for a researcher with clear potential for research excellence who thrives in and is inspired by interdisciplinary collaboration. The ideal candidate will be expected to contribute to high-quality research in their field while embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven inquiry and interdisciplinary dialogue. The successful candidate should have a strong and promising research profile, with potential for attracting external research funding, and a demonstrated ability to work across disciplines. The candidate will be attached to both the Department and DIAS, and should be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU. Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard assistant professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research, interdisciplinary exchange, active participation in DIAS and leadership activities. 

 

We seek a researcher with expertise in the field of medicinal chemistry, who is eager to develop their research career within the DIAS framework. The researcher should contribute to expanding and strengthening the interface between medicinal chemistry and pharmacy at SDU, fostering interdisciplinary research and collaboration across these fields. Alongside this disciplinary focus, the successful candidate should be intellectually curious about research beyond their immediate field and motivated to participate in DIAS’s wider cross-faculty community.

 

We particularly welcome applicants whose research combines medicinal chemistry disciplines with pharmaceutical sciences, including drug delivery, formulation, biopharmaceutics, or translational drug development. We are especially interested in researchers who can establish innovative research directions that connect molecular drug design and optimization with pharmaceutical development and therapeutic translation. The ideal candidate should demonstrate: 

 

• 
A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue.

• 
A strong commitment to interdisciplinary collaboration, contributing to research that bridges multiple fields. 

• 
A strong interest in driving internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

• 
Active engagement in various forms of research dissemination, including interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

• 
The ability to communicate project results in English both in writing in academic contexts and to the broader public.

• 
The ability to teach and supervise students.

 

Qualifications

Successful applicants must: 

• 
Hold a PhD or similar qualifications within relevant fields of medicinal chemistry, chemical biology and pharmacy (to qualify for the position as Assistant Professor you must have obtained a PhD or similar degree by the application deadline). 

• 
Exhibit curiosity-driven research excellence, thinking beyond traditional boundaries. 

• 
Be fluent in English.

• 
Show potential for attracting external research funding. Experience in applying for external funding and a strong international network are considered comparative advantages.

• 
Have research publications that demonstrate their excellence and broad thinking. 

• 
Be an inspiring and engaging teacher and supervisor.

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. DIAS fellows become members of the DIAS Society of Fellows, which supports research, networking, and leadership opportunities while fostering a sense of community among early-career researchers from diverse disciplines. The Society provides guidance and support to all Fellows, ensuring they feel welcome and integrated. DIAS also offers Blue Sky Mentoring. Together, these provide support for fellows’ development and integration into the DIAS community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.  

 

The Department

At the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, we contribute to solving some of society’s greatest challenges within energy, environment, health, and sustainability. We succeed because we build bridges between disciplines and transcend traditional boundaries. Our interdisciplinary mindset is not only a fundamental condition, but also our strength. And it is a strength that ensures our research and education are recognized both nationally and internationally.

 

Our vision is to create and apply knowledge across the natural sciences. We are unique in housing research within physics, chemistry, and pharmacy under one department, which provides excellent opportunities to explore the intersections between these disciplines.

 

But we go further. At SDU, we collaborate with researchers from IMADA (Department of Mathematics and Computer Science) to advance fields towards digital transformation. We work with IGT (Department of Green Technology) and MMI (Maersk Mc-Kinney Møller Institute) to harness the potential at the intersection of research and technological application. We also collaborate with researchers from the Faculty of Health Sciences to integrate health-related perspectives.

 

Additional information

For further information about being a fellow at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk. 

 

For more questions about the position please contact Head of Department Professor Jacob Kongsted, email: kongsted@sdu.dk. 

 

Application, salary, and employment terms

The position is based at the Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy in Odense and includes regular participation in DIAS and interdisciplinary collaboration.

Employment is governed by the collective agreement between the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

The salary comprises a seniority-based base salary and a centrally agreed supplement.

Additional supplements may be negotiated locally.

As of 1 August 2026, the annual salary for an Assistant Professor is DKK 480,224.96 (salary level 6), consisting of a base salary of DKK 417,456 and a supplement of DKK 62,768.96.

All amounts are stated before tax, before added pension (18.07%), and any additional supplements. Pension contributions are paid by SDU, and both salary components (the annual salary and the supplement) are pensionable. For more details on salary and taxation, please refer to the provided links about salary and taxation. International researchers may be eligible for the Danish Researcher Tax Scheme, which can offer favourable tax conditions. SDU can provide information and guidance regarding the scheme.

 

Danish Tenure Track Programme

An appointment as Assistant Professor (Danish tenure track) is limited to a six-year term. The academic assessment for promotion to Associate Professor must be initiated no later than the end of the fifth year of employment. However, a tenure track assistant professor may request an earlier assessment within the first four years.

If the initial assessment is negative, one reassessment may be conducted during the final six months prior to a potential transition. A maximum of two assessments may be undertaken.

A positive assessment leads to appointment to a permanent Associate Professor position. If the final assessment is negative, the employment may be terminated in accordance with the applicable collective agreement.

A six-year development plan for the tenure track programme is established at the start of employment.

 

Application requirements
The application must include the following:

• 
Letter of motivation that clearly explains the applicant's interest, qualifications, and motivation for the position.

• 
Detailed CV including documentation of experience, and contacts for possible references. 

• 
An elaborated research and funding plan (max 4 pages) for the next three years, including a description of synergy with the department's activities and how the applicant’s research could benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment. Applicants should also explain, in their letter of motivation, how they would contribute to DIAS’s intellectual community and engage with researchers beyond their immediate field. 

• 
Copies of certificates/Diplomas (Master and PhD degree).

• 
Complete list of publications, indicating which publications are most relevant for the position.

• 
Up to 5 of the most relevant research articles – if you submit a monograph, it counts as 3 articles. Please upload a pdf for each publication. For co-authored publications, briefly describe the extent of the co-authorship or your contribution to the publications (please do this for each co-authored publication). You can do so by using this form or by describing the co-authorship in such a way that the committee can assess the extent of your contribution.

• 
Applicants are requested to submit a teaching portfolio with the application as documentation for teaching experience as well as supervision qualifications. Formal application instructions and a guide for the teaching portfolio can be found here.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you can find information and facts about moving to, working and living in Denmark.

Application deadline: 25.02.2027

D’ANGLETERRE IS SEARCHING FOR A FULL-TIME DOORMAN

At d’Angleterre, the guest experience begins before a guest even steps inside the hotel.

We are looking for a warm, confident and attentive Doorman to join our Front Office team. As one of the first people our guests meet and one of the last they see when they leave, you play an important role in creating the lasting impression they take with them.

This role is about much more than opening doors. You represent d’Angleterre through genuine hospitality, personal recognition and an ability to anticipate what each guest may need.

ABOUT THE JOB

As our Doorman, you will create seamless and personalised arrival and departure experiences while ensuring the hotel entrance operates smoothly.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Welcoming hotel, restaurant and event guests with warmth and genuine personal attention

• Recognising returning guests and anticipating individual needs

• Opening hotel and car doors, assisting with luggage and guiding guests to their destination

• Parking and retrieving guest vehicles safely and handling keys with care

• Coordinating taxis, transfers and guest movement with Concierge, Reception and the luggage team

• Staying informed about arrivals, departures, VIP guests and inhouse events to help personalise the experience

• Sharing relevant guest preferences and requests with colleagues to ensure seamless service

• Providing knowledgeable information about the hotel and Copenhagen

• Maintaining a welcoming, polished and safe hotel entrance

• Taking ownership of guest requests and consistently representing the service and discretion expected at d’Angleterre

ABOUT YOU

You have a natural ability to make people feel welcome. You are warm and approachable while remaining polished, professional and attentive to detail.

Experience from a luxury hotel or another high-end guest-facing environment is preferred, but your personality and instinct for hospitality are just as important.

You remain calm in a busy environment, communicate confidently in English and enjoy working as part of a team. Danish and other languages are an advantage, as is a good knowledge of Copenhagen.

A valid driving licence suitable for driving guest vehicles in Denmark is required, and you must be comfortable parking different types of vehicles.

The position includes flexible shifts across days, afternoons and weekends.

WE OFFER

You will join one of Copenhagen’s most iconic luxury hotels and become part of an ambitious team dedicated to creating exceptional and personalised guest experiences.

As Doorman, you hold a particularly visible place within that experience.

You are not simply standing at the entrance to d’Angleterre. You are representing it.

ABOUT HOTEL D’ANGLETERRE

For more than 265 years, Hotel d’Angleterre has welcomed guests in the heart of Copenhagen. Today, we continue to combine our heritage with an ambition to develop and set new standards for luxury hospitality.

We believe exceptional service is ultimately about how we make people feel. And often, that experience begins with the person at the door.

Are you an inspiring and hands-on leader with a passion for luxury hospitality, impeccable standards and creating exceptional guest experiences?

We offer

You will join one of Scandinavia's most iconic luxury hotels and take responsibility for a department that plays a defining role in the d’Angleterre experience.

Here, tradition and high standards go hand in hand with a genuine ambition to continuously evolve. You will have the opportunity to shape Housekeeping operations, develop people and processes, and contribute directly to the quality of the hotel and the experiences we create for our guests.

You will become part of an ambitious and professional environment where personalised service, development and mutual respect are at the heart of everything we do.

At Hotel d’Angleterre, we believe that exceptional luxury starts with the people behind it.

Do you have an interest in Finance and want to apply your theoretical knowledge in an ambitious, international and dynamic organization? We are looking for a curious and structured student to join Orifarm as a Student Assistant in our Tax & Risk Management team

About the job

As a Student Assistant in Tax & Transfer Pricing, you will gain hands-on experience with key tax processes in a rapidly growing organization with a strong profile in the international market. You will join our Group Finance Team and work closely with ambitious colleagues.

You will work independently on various tasks after thorough training. You will always have access to help and sparring if needed. The working hours will be approximately 15 hours per week, with flexibility to accommodate your studies.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Preparing Transfer Pricing documentation

• Preparing tax returns

• Supporting monthly and quarterly transfer pricing calculations and adjustments

• Participating in process improvements and digitalization initiatives

• Reporting financial data to various authorities

• Various ad-hoc assignments

Who are you?

We are looking for an ambitious student who is currently enrolled in a bachelor’s or master’s degree programme in Economics (e.g., HA, HA(jur.), Cand.merc, or Finansbachelor).

We would like you to be analytical and good with numbers, providing a structured approach and the ability to maintain a good overview. You are also curious by nature and not afraid to ask questions. We value someone who is a team player and has a positive mindset. Additionally, you are able to work independently and take ownership of your tasks and responsibilities.

Who are we?

Our Global Finance team consists of 65 employees based in Odense, Poland and Czech Republic. You will be a part of the Tax & Risk Management team in Odense, consisting of 3 employees, and we have the global responsibility for all finance processes, reporting and controlling.

The team is characterized by a high degree of collaboration and mutual support. We work closely together, openly share challenges, and help one another navigate complex topics. You will work with our dedicated colleagues in an open office environment, which allows us to have a friendly and informal atmosphere.

You will join 70 other talented student assistants from diverse educational backgrounds as part of our Student Network Orifarm (SNO). SNO organizes social and professional events, allowing you to expand your network and connect with other students across functions.

Why should you work for Orifarm?

At Orifarm, we are 2,300 employees united by a shared purpose: improving access to affordable medicine for the people who need it. Founded in Odense, Denmark in 1994 by Birgitte & Hans Bøgh-Sørensen, we have built our business on challenging conventional thinking to make affordable high-quality pharmaceuticals more accessible across Europe. Rather than developing new medicines, we focus on finding smarter ways to bring existing treatments to patients, creating value for pharmacies, healthcare systems, and society.

We live by the mindset Challenge Accepted. It reflects our explorer spirit and can-do attitude, where challenges are perceived as opportunities. We encourage people to ask questions, challenge assumptions, and take ownership. Across teams, functions, and markets, you will find a collaborative and supportive culture built on trust, respect, and a flat hierarchy where everyone has a voice and direct access to decision-makers.

When you join Orifarm, you will be empowered to make a real impact from day one. We offer autonomy and great opportunities for career advancement, giving you a valuable start to your career. As our student assistant, you may have the opportunity to complete an internship or collaborate with us on your bachelor’s or master’s thesis. We value flexibility and provide a hybrid work model with the possibility of working from home two days a week.

We invite you to join Orifarm, if you are curious, ambitious, and accept the challenge of making affordable healthcare accessible.

We encourage everyone to apply

At Orifarm, we welcome people from all backgrounds, recognizing that the best outcomes come from a diverse and inclusive work environment. Our commitment is to create an environment where different perspectives and skills drive innovation and contribute to a sustainable future. By creating such an environment, we are confident that we can achieve better results together.

jobs.occupation: SMD Operators for a New Evening Shift
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced SMD Operator with a keen eye for quality, stable processes and precision-driven electronics manufacturing? Do you thrive in a technical environment where you take responsibility, work in a structured manner and actively contribute to a strong team? Then you could be our next experienced SMD Operator at NECAS A/S.

About the position
As an SMD Operator at NECAS, you will play a key role in the operation of our SMD lines – the heart of our electronics manufacturing. You will be responsible for setting up, monitoring and optimising processes, ensuring that production meets our high quality standards.
The electronics you help produce are used in everything from industrial and marine applications to defence and aerospace – industries where precision and reliability are essential.
You will become part of a highly skilled team and report to the Team Leader.

Your responsibilities
SMD line operation and preparation

• Operate and monitor SMD equipment, including solder paste printer, SPI, pick-and-place, AOI and reflow oven
• Prepare the line for production changeovers, including programmes, materials, feeder setup and documentation
• Ensure stable operation in accordance with production plans and work instructions
• Work with supporting processes such as the washing machine and stencil cleaner

Quality and inspection

• Carry out process and quality inspections, including visual inspection and First Article Inspection
• Analyse AOI results and respond to deviations
• Ensure the correct handling of materials and components, including batch control, traceability and shelf life
• Work in accordance with the IPC-A-610 standard (certification provided where required)
• Record defects and deviations in the quality management system

Collaboration and continuous improvement

• Ensure good communication and effective handovers between shifts
• Share knowledge and support colleagues in their daily work
• Contribute suggestions for improving processes and workflows
• Maintain order and structure in the SMD area in accordance with 5S principles

About you
We are looking for a candidate who already has solid experience in SMD production and is able to work independently in a technically demanding role.

We expect you to:

• Have a minimum of 3 years' experience with SMD equipment or electronics manufacturing
• Be structured and able to maintain an overview, even during busy periods
• Take responsibility and respond quickly when something deviates from the standard
• Be a team player who contributes positively to the team
• Have a technical understanding and an interest in working with advanced equipment
• Language: good command of English, spoken and written

What we offer
At NECAS, you will become part of a growing company where quality and professional expertise are at the heart of what we do. You will receive:

• A thorough introduction to our processes and equipment
• Opportunities for relevant training and certifications, such as IPC-A-610
• A strong team environment and an informal culture with a high level of professional expertise
• A workplace in Støvring's newest industrial area, close to the E45 motorway
• Competitive terms of employment, including pension and health insurance

About NECAS
NECAS is one of Denmark's leading EMS companies, manufacturing electronics for the industrial, marine/offshore, defence, aerospace and scientific sectors – industries where quality and precision are essential.
We are one of the few EMS manufacturers in Denmark with AS9100 certification for the aerospace industry. At NECAS, you will become part of a company experiencing significant growth, where you can develop your professional skills and help push the boundaries of Danish electronics manufacturing.

As we say: Built for trust.

How to apply
The position will be filled as soon as possible. We are inviting candidates to interviews on an ongoing basis, so please send your application and CV as soon as possible. We read all applications and will contact candidates we would like to get to know better.
If you have any questions, please contact Team Leader Mariana Surleac on +45 92 92 76 20.
